decisions.reason: The source constrains the SPS30 module's SEL pin on the sensor board but does not change any power-board-to-main-board or main-board-to-sensor-board connector.
The source necessarily adds a physical SPS30 module-interface constraint: pin 4 (SEL) must be hardwired to GND on the PCB rather than left floating or driven HIGH.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text: one thing just we need to make sure, is SPS30 pin 4 (SEL) hardwired to GND on the PCB? This is critical, if SEL floats or goes HIGH, the SPS30 switches to UART mode and won't respond on I2C

value_updates.sps30_sel_pin_connection: pin 4 (SEL) hardwired to GND on the PCB

decisions.reason: The SPS30 SEL connection selects I2C versus UART mode; it does not change the established 3.3V logic-level compatibility or level-shifter policy.
The SPS30 SEL pin is unrelated to the ESP32 BOOT and reset circuitry.
Selecting the SPS30 I2C mode does not alter which power rails are monitored, the monitoring IC, or measurement coverage.
Hardwiring the SPS30 SEL pin to GND does not change the switched 5V rail, its GPIO control, or its powered loads.
The SPS30 communication-mode selection does not change the standalone USB regulator, source selection, or 3.3V load requirement.
The source ensures that SPS30 uses I2C but does not change bus speed, pull-ups, cable length, or signal-conditioning values.
The SPS30 SEL connection has no effect on addressable LED supply voltage or data-level logic.
The source does not change the DCDC1 configured voltage or the required regulated 3.3V rail.
The SPS30 mode-selection pin is unrelated to the panel-mounted power-button connector and PWRON line.
The source does not alter the ESP32 module choice, breakout-hole placement, full pin access, or breakout pitch.
